text.p: Former England international Alan Ball, who resigned as manager of first division Manchester City 10 days ago, said on Friday he might quit soccer.

Ball, a member of the England side which won the 1966 World Cup, managed City for a year. They were relegated at the end of last season and had lost two of their first three matches of the new season when Ball resigned.
"At this moment in time, I think I'll be history," Ball said in his first public comment since his departure from City.
"I'm looking forward to having my own space. It's not that I've fallen out of love with the game but I think it's about time that I looked at something else.
"If something does come up then I'll think about it but, at this moment in time, I'm not in that frame of mind."
